typography.$description: Showrun Media typography — v1.1.0, locked 2026-08-07. Three families, three jobs. Chosen against four constraints in order: (1) it must RENDER ON A COLLABORATOR'S MACHINE, because cue sheets, briefs and working Sheets get shared and Google Docs has no font-upload path — so every family here is on Google Fonts; (2) it must be readable at 14px in a dense table; (3) it must flex — real weight range and true italics, so a setting can be dialled in without the skeleton changing; (4) the display face must contrast the body face rather than echo it. All three are SIL OFL: free for commercial use, embeddable, redistributable, no vendor licence to police.

display.$description: Headlines, oversized numerals, section titles. Grotesque with masthead authority. Variable: wght 100–900 plus a wdth axis 62–125, so condensed-editorial and wide-poster come out of one file. Replaces Switzer, which is Fontshare and therefore cannot render in a shared Google Doc.

body.$description: All running text, captions, table content. Locked first and independently: at 54.6% it carries the highest x-height of any candidate, which is what keeps 14px cue text legible. Variable wght 100–900 with true italics.

mono.$description: Labels, values, times, cue states, running heads, title blocks. NEVER a display or heading face. Taller x-height (55%) and rounder counters than the alternatives, so digits stay open rather than packing tight — chosen on how it holds a TIME column and a call-sheet key/value strip, not on a specimen. Variable wght 100–800 with true italics. Replaces Martian Mono, which has NO ITALIC at all — a functional gap, since a held or soft cue must not look like a hard one.

$extensions.showrun.availability: All three are on Google Fonts, verified against the CSS2 API. This is a hard requirement, not a preference: a shared Sheet or Doc renders with the recipient's fallback otherwise, and the design silently breaks on someone else's screen.
$extensions.showrun.retired: Switzer, Cabinet Grotesk, General Sans, Supreme (all Fontshare, not on Google Fonts). Martian Mono (no italic). Instrument Serif (single weight, no range). IBM Plex Mono was the runner-up for mono and lost on character, not capability — it packs digits tighter and reads more like instrumentation; JetBrains keeps a TIME column more open.

display.$description: Archivo at 800 for headlines. The variable axis reaches 900; 800 holds more counter shape at large sizes.

body.$description: Inter 400 for running text. Its x-height carries the weight Switzer needed 500 to reach.

label.$description: JetBrains Mono 600 for labels; 700 for a cue state that must read as a command. Italic 400 for a held or soft cue.

numeral.$description: Oversized stat treatment. One per slide.

size.$description: Proven for slides only. These are not a general type scale — see the geometry note in the brand kit; a cue sheet, a one-sheet and a web page do not share one.

body.$description: 17px x 1.62 = 27.54px, which is where the 28px baseline grid comes from. That grid is the one piece of geometry that is actually derived rather than chosen.

axes.$description: Variable axes available, and what each is for. Using them is how the system flexes without adding families.

displayWidth.$description: Archivo wdth. Below 100 for condensed editorial headlines; above for wide poster settings. Default 100.

monoWeight.$description: JetBrains Mono is variable, unlike the IBM Plex alternative that was considered alongside it.
